claims.subject: Static Adversary
claims.evidence_quote: We assume the presence of a static adversary, which pre-selects the faulty nodes before the algorithm begins1 While the adversary cannot change which nodes are faulty once the execution starts, it can decide when and how these nodes crash.

claims.subject: Adaptive Adversary
claims.evidence_quote: In contrast, an adaptive adversary determines faulty nodes during the algorithm’s execution.

claims.subject: Distributed Trigger Counting with Crash-Fault
claims.evidence_quote: The message complexity of an algorithm is the total number of messages sent by all the nodes throughout the execution of the algorithm.

claims.subject: CONGEST Communication Model
claims.evidence_quote: We consider CONGEST communication model [10], where a node is allowed to send a message of size O(log n) bits through an edge per round.

claims.subject: Fault-Tolerant Distributed Trigger Counting
claims.evidence_quote: Consider a complete network with n nodes, in which at most f nodes could be faulty and the remaining (n − f ) nodes are non-faulty.

claims.subject: Fault-Tolerant Distributed Trigger Counting
claims.evidence_quote: In the explicit setting, the algorithm accounts for all triggers across the entire graph, whereas in the implicit setting, a subset of processors is responsible for counting the triggers.
